    The centre corner of E₈ in characteristic two (Appendix B) #

    characteristic-two-mesh-calculations.tex. In R₅ = k⟨x, y⟩/(x⁵, y³, (x + y)²) over a ring with 2 = 0, put ω₃ = yx³y, ω₄ = yx⁴y, ω₅ = ω₄x³y. "The following words span R₅: xⁱ, xⁱyxʲ (j ≤ 4), xⁱω₃, xⁱω₄xʲ (j ≤ 3), xⁱω₅. Their span contains 1 and is closed under multiplication on the right by x, y. … The highest word degree in the list is fourteen." We prove the closure (spn_mul_x, spn_mul_y), so that every word of degree n lies in the span spn n of the listed words of degree n, and spn n = 0 for n ≥ 15.
